performances.jam: A nicely stretched out version of a typical outro in this classic pairing of "Fee" > "Maze."

The outro sticks to the "Fee" framework until 9 minutes when Fish picks up the beat, leading to an upbeat segment filled with the blissfull, atmospheric style of jamming that is so representative of the '99 sound.  Eventually returns to Earth at 20 minutes and winds down to close.  In the realm of "Fee" jams, this weasel reigns supreme.
Similar to the typical harmonics-laced outro, but Fish is more active and Trey's playing is also atypical.
Outro evolves into a beautiful calypso style jam that grows more abstract with delay effects. -> into "Taste."
"Maze" tease in a jam that sticks close to the normal outro with an added repeating riff from Trey.  Page also contributes on the synthesizer before the  -> into "Timber."

Like 7/5/98, a vocal flub leads to an extended outro jam that quickly moves beyond the norm. Page's ambient effects and Trey's use of the whammy pedal combine to create a jam reminiscent of the late '90's sound.
First appearance of the megaphone since 2/25/97.  Also includes sirens at the beginning and end of the song.
Sirens over a rolling outro with nice contributions from Mike and Page. > to "Makisupa Policeman."
Another stretched out, harmonics-filled outro with added sirens and synthesizer. Excellent -> to "Time Turns Elastic."
A serene outro, similar to 7/29/03. > into "Backwards Down the Number Line."
This patient and cohesive jam covers a lot of ground in a relatively short period of time. Excellent and Must-Hear.
Slightly extended outro with nice melodic contributions from Mike. > to "Maze".
